sections.history: Tiruvendurai, at Cherivadi Vaikal about 10 km from Mannargudi on the road to Thiruthuraipoondi, is a Paadal Petra Sthalam hymned in the Tevaram by Tirugnana Sambandar, in Tiruvarur district. Its historical name is Tiruventhurai; the stone temple is of the Chola period and later, keeping the form of the Shiva shrines of the Tiruvarur delta.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian delta temple, the shrine enshrines Vandurainathar — also Vanduthurainathar, Brahmapureeswarar, Pramareswarar — in the sanctum, with the goddess Vel Nedunganni (also named Sathyadayi) in her own shrine, a Nandi and the parivara devatas about the prakara. An Ardhanariswarar figure appears in the local tradition. The walled courtyard keeps the form of the delta temples.
sections.legends: The sthala legend tells of the sage Bringhi, who in his devotion wished to circle only Shiva, and took the form of a bee (bhringa) to pass between the lord and the goddess; angered, Parvati did penance, and the lord granted her his half as Ardhanariswarar. Shiva is worshipped here as Vandurainathar — Brahmapureeswarar — with Vel Nedunganni beside him. As with many delta shrines, the fuller sthala purana survives in local tradition and the Tevaram verses.
sections.festivals: The temple observes Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship, at the quiet scale of a village shrine. Pilgrims of the Mannargudi–Thiruthuraipoondi tract include Tiruvendurai among their stops.
sections.experience: At Tiruvendurai the pilgrim comes to a quiet shrine of the Tiruvarur delta. Before Vandurainathar and Vel Nedunganni, the visitor finds the unhurried grace of a Tevaram temple, and the memory of the bee-sage Bringhi and the lord's gift of his half to the goddess.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Tiruvendurai is at Cherivadi Vaikal, about 10 km from Mannargudi on the road to Thiruthuraipoondi, in Tiruvarur district. Mannargudi and Thiruthuraipoondi are the nearest towns, with buses and taxis to the village; Tiruvarur is the nearest rail head.
